boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby San Antonio corridors, each with one source-backed reason to stop.

cards.title: Japanese Tea Garden: free garden paths
cards.subtitle: N. St. Mary’s Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter from N. St. Mary’s Street and follow the garden paths, waterfall, pagoda, and koi ponds; use the upper areas if step-free access is needed.
cards.short_summary: A free, daily-open garden destination beside the zoo.
cards.evidence_claim: The Japanese Tea Garden at 3853 N. St. Mary’s Street is open daily from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7 a.m.–5 p.m.; upper garden and pavilion are ramp-accessible, while the lower garden is reached by stairs.

cards.title: San Antonio Zoo: animal habitats
cards.subtitle: N. St. Mary’s Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the zoo’s current visit page to select a date and ticket, then plan around the listed animal presentations and other daily happenings.
cards.short_summary: A 50-plus-acre zoo with current daily programming.
cards.evidence_claim: San Antonio Zoo is at 3903 N. St. Mary’s Street and publishes ticket options and daily happenings for visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit – San Antonio Zoo
cards.access_notes: The official visit page lists 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and directs visitors to current ticket options.

cards.title: Kiddie Park: preserved 1920s rides
cards.subtitle: N. St. Mary’s Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the operating-day schedule before heading over; the park preserves original rides including its Ferris wheel and hand-carved carousel.
cards.short_summary: A historic children’s amusement park now at the zoo address.
cards.evidence_claim: Kiddie Park, at 3903 N. St. Mary’s Street, preserves original rides including a Ferris wheel and Herschell Spillman carousel.
cards.access_notes: The official contact page lists Friday–Sunday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Monday–Thursday as closed.

cards.title: Sunken Garden Theater: open-air stage
cards.subtitle: N. St. Mary’s Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the venue calendar before making the trip, then photograph the historic open-air amphitheater from the N. St. Mary’s Street entrance.
cards.short_summary: A historic amphitheater in a former quarry.
cards.evidence_claim: Sunken Garden Theater is a historic open-air amphitheater at 3875 N. St. Mary’s Street that hosts public concerts and food festivals.
cards.source_title: Brackenridge Park Conservancy: Things to See & Do
cards.access_notes: Event access and pricing vary; confirm the current event listing and venue policies before arrival.

cards.title: Brackenridge Park: river and trails
cards.subtitle: N. St. Mary’s Street corridor
cards.notes: Start at the N. St. Mary’s Street edge, then choose a self-guided walk, picnic, or riverside pause within the historic public park.
cards.short_summary: A large historic park with the San Antonio River running through it.
cards.evidence_claim: Brackenridge Park at 3910 N. St. Mary’s Street includes a stretch of the San Antonio River and opportunities for picnics, jogging, and fishing.
cards.access_notes: Use the park’s posted rules and any temporary closure notices when planning an outdoor visit.

cards.title: Witte Museum: nature, science, culture
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around the museum’s current daily demonstrations, and use the Broadway-facing H-E-B Lantern Entrance after parking nearby.
cards.short_summary: A Brackenridge Park museum with science and culture displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The Witte Museum is at 3801 Broadway in Brackenridge Park and presents nature, science, and culture programming with daily demonstrations.
cards.access_notes: Current general admission and day-specific hours are posted on the museum’s visit page; visitor parking is free.

cards.title: Pioneer Hall: Texas Centennial landmark
cards.subtitle: Avenue B corridor, beside the Witte Museum
cards.notes: Pair this exterior stop with the nearby Witte Museum and look for the limestone building with red tile roof immediately north of the museum.
cards.short_summary: A designated archaeological landmark within Brackenridge Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Pioneer Hall, immediately north of the Witte Museum, was built in 1937 as a memorial to Texas pioneers, trail drivers, and rangers.
cards.access_notes: This card is for viewing the named historic building from the surrounding park; follow posted site and museum access guidance.

cards.title: The DoSeum: learn by doing
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor near Mulberry
cards.notes: Use the museum’s current visitor information before going, then focus the visit on its hands-on exhibit halls and outdoor exhibit yards.
cards.short_summary: A children’s museum designed around interactive learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The DoSeum is at 2800 Broadway near Mulberry and is a children’s museum where learning centers on doing, creating, and tinkering.
cards.source_title: United Way of San Antonio: The DoSeum
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s official site for current admission, timed-entry, and hours information before visiting.

cards.title: Botanical Garden: seasonal landscapes
cards.subtitle: N. New Braunfels Avenue corridor at Funston Place
cards.notes: Enter from Funston Place and use the garden’s current map and seasonal hours to structure a plant-focused visit through the grounds.
cards.short_summary: A garden destination at the Funston and North New Braunfels corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The San Antonio Botanical Garden is at the northeast corner of Funston Place and North New Braunfels Avenue, at 555 Funston Place.
cards.source_title: San Antonio Botanical Garden: Directions & Parking
cards.access_notes: Hours change seasonally; the garden publishes current seasonal hours and limited free on-site parking for guests.

cards.title: McNay Art Museum: art and sculpture grounds
cards.subtitle: N. New Braunfels Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Bring Trinity identification for the institution’s student-admission benefit, then allow time for galleries and the outdoor sculpture grounds.
cards.short_summary: An art museum whose student partnership includes Trinity University.
cards.evidence_claim: McNay Art Museum is at 6000 N. New Braunfels Avenue; Trinity University students, faculty, and staff receive free general admission through its educational partnership.
cards.access_notes: Bring qualifying Trinity identification for free general admission; special exhibitions may have a separate charge.
